heading: Boat type and propulsion
points: What type of boat will be used for the trip?
Will the vessel be powered solely by motor or also include paddles?
What is expected of passengers on transfers and on dedicated outings?
intro: The same tour label can describe different boats and different roles for passengers. Ask whether the proposed segment is paddled, motorized or a combination, and who provides the effort. Confirm the details for both transfers and dedicated outings. Choose the arrangement that fits your interest rather than assuming canoe always means active paddling.

heading: Boarding and seating
points: What is the exact procedure for getting aboard the boat?
Where will passengers be located once on board?
How many passengers share the boat and what seating is provided?
intro: Boarding and time in the boat are part of the experience, so ask about them before choosing. Request the actual passenger arrangement, type of seat and starting point. Explain any requirements your group has for getting aboard or sitting. A scenic regional photograph cannot confirm those details or demonstrate suitability for your group.

heading: Actual water route
points: What is the exact trajectory the vessel will follow?
Where will we pass and which rivers or channels will we transit?
Are there scheduled stops along the route?
intro: Ask the provider to name the route and distinguish the departure point, observation areas and finishing point. Check whether stops are included and how the journey returns to your base. Conditions can require a different plan; confirm who explains any change and which alternatives belong to your booking rather than assuming unrestricted access.

heading: Guiding and group
points: Who will be the guide accompanying the group?
How many visitors share the boat and guide?
How will interaction with the group be managed during the trip?
intro: Find out who leads the outing and how many people share the boat and guide. Guiding language, explanation and time at stops can matter as much as the scenery. If you want photography or focused observation, discuss that beforehand. Confirm any private arrangements explicitly; a private room does not make the boat or guide private.

heading: Effort and alternatives
points: What level of physical effort is required on the journey?
Are there options to rest if the pace is intense?
Which alternative activities can be confirmed for this booking?
intro: Describe the pace and effort your group wants, then ask how the actual outing compares. Confirm expected paddling, walking between segments and time seated in the boat. Ask about alternatives without assuming they exist or are included. If an activity does not match your needs, get a specific answer before accepting the proposed program.

heading: Written inclusions
points: What elements are explicitly included in the final price?
Are entries to specific sites contemplated?
Is land transport to the water exit included?
intro: Read the water outing as part of the whole package. Match starting and finishing points with road transfers, accommodation and onward travel. Check what equipment and guiding are included and what costs extra. Keep the provider’s change terms alongside the itinerary so a different route or cancelled outing does not leave the arrangements unclear.
